# SMAIL (Saudi Medical AI Lab)

> SMAIL is an open, volunteer-driven research program that connects students at Saudi universities with experienced mentors worldwide to conduct AI-for-health research. The program is supervised by the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) and licensed by the National Center for Non-Profit Sector (License No. 1100542400).

SMAIL runs cohort-based mentorship: students are paired with mentors from top universities and institutions for hands-on medical AI research, with the goal of producing first-author research papers. The program is officially 6 months, expects roughly 15 hours/week of student commitment, and is currently open only to students enrolled at Saudi universities.

Current program stats: 20+ mentors, 31+ students, cohorts ongoing.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://smail.org.sa/): Program overview, mission, statistics, application periods for students and mentors, and sponsorship information.
- [Students](https://smail.org.sa/students.html): Profiles of students in the SMAIL program by cohort.
- [Mentors](https://smail.org.sa/mentors.html): Profiles of mentors guiding SMAIL research by cohort.
- [Staff](https://smail.org.sa/staff.html): The team running SMAIL, plus staff alumni.
- [Publications](https://smail.org.sa/papers.html): Accepted and published research papers co-authored by SMAIL students and mentors.
- [FAQ](https://smail.org.sa/FAQ.html): Answers to common questions about program length, time commitment, eligibility, and publication outcomes.
